newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to form French dealer subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Renault to form French dealer subsidiary.

text.p: Carmaker Renault said on Wednesday it would create a subsidiary in July, Renault France Automobiles, to run its 77 French dealerships and bring the 10,000 staff under the same collective agreement.

The creation of the new subsidiary is designed to accelerate the dealers' response time to market shifts and their return to profit, Renault said in a statement. Its 77 French dealerships generated 26 percent of its sales in France last year.
Fifty-three of the dealerships are company branches employing 8,600 staff covered by the metallurgical collective agreement. They had a combined operating loss of 247 million francs last year.

The other 24 dealerships are structured as corporate subsidiaries and their 1,400 workers are covered by the automotive services collective agreement. The subsidiaries traditionally perform better than the branches but Renault did not break out their 1996 results.
The entire Renault group posted a 5.25 billion franc loss for 1996, including 3.9 billion in charges, and has embarked on aggressive cost-cutting moves.
It said it would present a plan "to ensure the survival" of its dealerships, including proposed synergies and a plan to change the branches' collective agreement, to the staff council on May 23.
"The plan will include a change in the collective agreement and the negotiation...of new accords," it said. "The establishment of Renault France Automobiles will not have an effect on jobs."
A spokeswoman said the plan aimed to bring all 10,000 workers under the automotive services collective agreement.

Renault's unions, already battling the planned closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium and the elimination of nearly 2,800 jobs in France this year, oppose putting the branches into a subsidiary or changing the collective agreement.

Chairman Louis Schweitzer said in March when he presented the group's 1996 results that he proposed to form a dealer subsidiary and negotiate a new contract, saying dealership staff do not work under the same conditions as car factory workers.
Renault aims to establish Renault France Automobiles on July 1, but the 24 subsidiaries will not immediately be part of the unit, the spokeswoman said.
